chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام: Is wudu (ablution) to be performed because of food, or drinking milk—the milks of camels, cattle, and sheep—and their urine and their meat? He said: Wudu (ablution) is not performed because of it.

key_terms.شُرْبِ: drinking or consumption as a beverage

ai.seo_question: Does eating meat or drinking camel, cow, or sheep milk require wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام regarding wudu (ablution) in relation to consuming certain animal products. It states that eating food or consuming the milk, urine, or meat of camels, cattle, and sheep does not require wudu (ablution).
